Hi Tom / Karen —

Thanks again for a productive call this morning. Quick recap + next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

Call summary:
- Use case: customer support triage + automated summary + sensitive data redaction.
- Expected QPS: ~30 reqs/sec peak, avg 10 reqs/sec.
- Primary concern: data residency and key management.
- Main integration constraints discussed: SSO (SAML/Okta), KMS/HSM for encryption of model inputs/outputs, and logging/retention policies (7 years for audit logs).

High-level recommendation (based on what we discussed):
- Hosted API: fastest to start but does not meet FintechCo KMS/HSM and long-term retention controls.
- Dedicated capacity: might work if we can surface KMS integration and log forwarding to your SIEM; still multitenant control plane.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): recommended if regulatory requirement is strict (customer stated SOC2 + internal audit requiring customer-managed keys and >5-year log retention).

Open questions / actions for FintechCo:
1) Can you confirm whether enterprise policy requires customer-managed KMS keys for model input encryption (yes/no)?
2) Who owns the SSO SAML metadata (IdP admin contact)?
3) Which SIEM/log archive endpoint should we plan to push logs to (Splunk/Seq/S3)? Retention SLA needed.

Action items (we'll take these):
- Dev (cc'd) to capture KMS/HSM integration options and initial network topology for Private deployment.
- I'll share a short security questionnaire and our private deployment diagram (attached).

Attachments: FintechCo_Security_Questionnaire_v1.pdf (filled), redwood_private_architecture.png (high-level).

Proposed next step: quick tech sync with your infra/security team — are you available Tue 10/6 or Wed 10/7?

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — good recap. A few answers and clarifications from our side: 

1) KMS/HSM: Yes, our security policy requires customer-managed keys for any storage of PII or transaction data. We currently use AWS KMS with CloudHSM for FIPS-backed key material.
2) SSO: Okta is our IdP. I can share the SAML metadata. Point of contact is Karen (cc'd).
3) Logging/Retention: Audit logs need to be retained for 7 years, but our infra team wants logs forwarded to our internal S3 archive and to Splunk for real-time alerts.

About deployment mode: initially we'd like a Dedicated pool for performance and cost predictability, but our security/compliance team is leaning toward Private (VPC) because of KMS and long retention. We wanted to understand what gaps would remain if we chose Dedicated (i.e., can Dedicated surface KMS integration and provide the 7-year retention?).

We can do a tech sync on Wed 10/7 at 10am PT — Karen and our infra lead will join.

- Tom
Head of Cloud Engineering
FintechCo

Hi all — quick technical notes ahead of Wed's sync. High-level: Dedicated can meet some but not all of your controls; Private is the only option that fully surfaces customer-managed KMS + long-term archival under your control. Details below.

Dedicated (what we can and can't do):
- Network: Dedicated pools run in Redwood-managed VPCs in customer-dedicated subnets; we support IP allowlists and private peering.
- KMS: We can encrypt at-rest with keys we manage. For customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key), we support envelope encryption via customer KMS only on Private deployments today. There is an in-progress feature for Dedicated to support customer KMS via a proxy, but it is not GA and would likely require an SOC/eng review and extra controls (timeline ~Q1 2027).
- Logging/Retention: Dedicated can forward structured logs to customer endpoints (Splunk, S3) for short-term retention (up to 1 year) as part of the service. Long-term archival (7+ years) requires you to manage the archive; we can forward to S3 bucket you own, but Continuous access for eDiscovery/audit has additional requirements.

Private (what it provides):
- Private control plane with customer VPC peering or on-prem install.
- Full customer KMS/HSM integration (CloudHSM, BYOK) for encrypting inputs and model data.
- Log forwarding directly into your SIEM/S3 under your retention policies.
- Optionally air-gapped on-prem packaging for regulated workloads.

Risks/considerations:
- Private setup has longer lead time (2–6 weeks for standard VPC deployments; on-prem longer) and higher onboarding engineering effort.
- Dedicated will be faster to provision (days) but may need engineering workarounds for BYOK and custom retention beyond 1 year.

Prep for Wed:
- Tom/Karen: please share the Okta SAML metadata and the S3 destination details + IAM role we should assume for log delivery.
- Marissa: I'll prepare a short architecture note comparing Dedicated vs Private with action items for compliance.

Thanks,
